source_documents.title: Room temperature phosphorescence of 2-phenylindole. Singlet-triplet absorption and phosphorescence quantum yield – complete resolution of Jablonski diagram

reference_evidence_units.quote: Direct absorption of the triplet state explains efficient phosphorescence seen in the conducted experiment.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2-phenylindole
reference_evidence_units.statement: Direct S0→T1 absorption populates T1 and gives efficient phosphorescence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The excitation at 405 nm results in a pure phosphorescence emission with a mean lifetime of 1.29 ms, see Fig. SM9 and [4].
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2-phenylindole
reference_evidence_units.statement: Pure RTP with a 1.29 ms mean lifetime.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The emission efficiency (quantum yield) of the triplet state is 0.35, estimated by comparison with the fluorescence of coumarin 152 in acetonitrile.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2-phenylindole

reference_evidence_units.quote: In rigid systems such as polymer films, where molecular motion is strongly restricted, fluorescence anisotropy reveals the relative orientation of the fluorescence and phosphorescence tran sition moments.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2-phenylindole
reference_evidence_units.statement: The rigid film fixes the molecules (used for anisotropy).
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Background statement; not a mechanism claim.

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
reference_mechanisms.rationale: RTP in PVA (1.29 ms, Φ 0.35) after direct singlet-triplet absorption; the paper resolves the full singlet/triplet scheme.
